newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico Cetes rate seen rising on peso weakness.
newsitem.headline: Mexico Cetes rate seen rising on peso weakness.

text.p: Mexico's bellwether one-month Cetes rate is seen rising up to 125 basis points at the primary auction on Tuesday, following recent pressure on the peso and the hike in the yield on the U.S. long bond, market analysts said.
"It is important that investors continue to receive a good return. The strong decline in rates in the last month has considerably reduced the real return offered to them," one dealer said.
During the month of August, the one-month Cetes yield fell 584 basis points to 24.38 percent last week.
Higher rates would help lift pressure on the peso, which has been hit by a rising yield on the U.S. 30-year bond. On Monday the yield was 7.12 percent.
The peso was also weakened by news of fresh attacks last week by guerrillas in several states in Mexico.
Analysts added that a seasonal rebound in inflation expected in September is also a factor that could help push up Cetes rates at the Banco de Mexico auction on Tuesday.
Banco de Mexico will auction 3.3 bilion worth of Cetes at the auction this week.
